stem: Give scientific reason: The geostationary satellites are not useful for studies of polar regions.
solution: A geostationary satellite revolves in an orbit that lies in the equatorial plane of the earth, at a height of about \(35780\) km, with a period of \(24\) hours so that it appears stationary over one point on the equator. From this equatorial position it can view mainly the equatorial and mid-latitude regions; the polar regions lie almost edge-on and are not properly covered. Hence geostationary satellites are not useful for studying the polar regions — for that, polar (sun-synchronous) satellites in low polar orbits are used.

stem: Give scientific reason: The hydrogenation of vegetable oil in presence of nickel catalyst forms Vanaspati-ghee.
solution: Vegetable oils are unsaturated compounds — they contain carbon–carbon double bonds (\(C = C\)). When such oils are heated with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst, an addition reaction takes place and the double bonds get saturated (converted to single bonds): \(C = C + H_2 \xrightarrow{Ni} C - C\). The saturated product is a semi-solid fat. Hence the hydrogenation of vegetable oil in presence of nickel catalyst forms Vanaspati-ghee.

stem: Give scientific reason: Atomic radius goes on increasing down the 'group'.
solution: On going down a group, a new shell (energy level) is added at every step, so the number of shells increases. As a result the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus increases, and the inner shells also screen (shield) the outer electrons from the nuclear pull. Even though the nuclear charge increases, the effect of the added shells and shielding dominates, so the outermost electrons are held less tightly. Hence the atomic radius goes on increasing down a group.

stem: What is meant by an 'alloy'? Give two examples.
solution: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal with a small quantity of a non-metal, prepared to obtain desired properties (such as greater hardness, strength or resistance to corrosion). Examples: (1) Brass — an alloy of copper and zinc; (2) Steel — an alloy of iron and carbon. (Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, is also acceptable.)

| Oxidation | Reduction |
|---|---|
| Addition of oxygen (or an electronegative element) to a substance. | Removal of oxygen (or an electronegative element) from a substance. |
| Removal of hydrogen (or an electropositive element) from a substance. | Addition of hydrogen (or an electropositive element) to a substance. |
| Loss of electrons by a species. | Gain of electrons by a species. |

For example, in \(2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO\), copper is oxidised; in \(CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O\), copper oxide is reduced.

stem: Give the molecular formula and structural formula of Benzene.
solution: Molecular formula of benzene: \(C_6H_6\). Structural formula: benzene is a cyclic (aromatic) hydrocarbon in which six carbon atoms form a regular hexagonal ring with alternate single and double bonds (\(C = C\) and \(C - C\)) between adjacent carbons, and one hydrogen atom attached to each carbon. It is usually drawn as a regular hexagon of six carbon atoms with three alternate double bonds (often represented by a hexagon with a circle inside to show the delocalised bonds).

stem: An electric tungsten bulb is connected into a home circuit. The home electric supply runs at \(220\) volt potential difference. When switched on, a current of \(0.45\ A\) flows through the bulb. What must be the power (wattage) of the bulb? If it is kept 'on' for \(10\) hours, how many units of electricity will be consumed?
solution:
Power of the bulb: \(P = V \times I = 220 \times 0.45 = 99\ W\). So the wattage of the bulb is about \(99\) W (nearly \(100\) W).

Energy consumed in \(10\) hours \(= P \times t = 99\ W \times 10\ h = 990\ Wh = 0.99\ kWh\). Since \(1\) unit of electricity \(= 1\ kWh\), the electricity consumed \(= 0.99\) unit (approximately \(1\) unit).

stem: 'A rainbow is the combined effect of refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection of light'. Explain the sentence.
solution: A rainbow is seen after rain when tiny water droplets remain suspended in the atmosphere and the sun is behind the observer. Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism and produces a rainbow through three effects: (1) Refraction and dispersion — when sunlight (white light) enters a droplet it bends (refracts) and splits into its seven constituent colours because different colours are refracted through different angles (dispersion). (2) Total internal reflection — these dispersed colours strike the inner back surface of the droplet at an angle greater than the critical angle and are totally internally reflected inside the drop. (3) Refraction again — as the colours leave the droplet they are refracted (and further dispersed) once more. The combined effect of these many droplets sends the separated colours to the observer's eye, forming the coloured arc of the rainbow (red on the outside, violet on the inside).
